title: Determinant of an endomorphism
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ a free $R$-module with a finite basis $(m_1,\dots,m_n)$. For an $R$-linear endomorphism $f:M\to M$, write $f(m_j)=\sum_ia_{ij}m_i$ with $a_{ij}\in R$; the determinant $\det(f\mid M)\in R$ is the determinant of the matrix $(a_{ij})\in M_n(R)$. It does not depend on the basis, since the matrices of $f$ in two bases are conjugate. In particular, for a field $K$ and a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $V$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], $\det(F\mid V)\in K$ is defined for every $K$-linear endomorphism $F$ of $V$, and $F$ is invertible if and only if $\det(F\mid V)\neq0$.
